document.title: Put all document presentation behind one portable renderer
document.summary: PRD and Design Solution own structured meaning, System Diagram owns system-diagram-v1 JSON-to-SVG, and HTML Report Designer validates both before filling one report template.
document.reviewFocus: Blocked until the current PRD revision receives explicit whole-document approval; meanwhile review the renderer seam, strict failure behavior, decision lifecycle, and dependency-free skill-relative path.

sections.title: The current PRD revision cannot authorize new design work

items: Upstream status

Existing system

Gate

sections.title: CWD-relative templates and parallel render paths made drift inevitable
sections.summary: The obvious approach—telling agents to copy the right template—cannot guarantee consistent output.

items: Ownership pressure
PRD/design skills mixed content policy with shell placeholders and CSS mechanics.
Portability pressure
Installed skills could not resolve repository-root scripts and assets from unrelated projects.
Consistency pressure
Separate template/CSS/runtime families evolved independently.
Trust pressure
Browser selections lacked an explicit canonical approval boundary.

sections.title: HTML Report Designer owns the sole rendering boundary

items: PRD
Owns required product roles, slices, acceptance, and product decision lifecycle.
Design Solution
Owns required architecture roles, seam, path, proof, and ADR consequences.
System Diagram
Owns evidence validation and bundled deterministic infrastructure JSON-to-SVG generation.
HTML Report Designer
Owns schema validation, block rendering, report template, CSS, navigation, review runtime, and report validation.
Human approver
Owns transition from Draft/Review/Proposed to Approved/Accepted.

blocks.title: No fallback path
blocks.text: A missing companion skill, invalid profile, absent System Diagram provenance, or incomplete approval blocks generation instead of producing a substitute artifact.

sections.title: Validated meaning crosses one rendering seam

items.title: Compose
items.text: PRD or Design Solution writes canonical-report-v1 JSON with required section roles, stable IDs, approval state, and decisions.

items.title: Generate
items.text: System Diagram validates a bounded question and renders retained system-diagram-v1 JSON into accessible infrastructure SVG.

items.title: Validate
items.text: The canonical renderer rejects unknown fields, missing roles, incomplete slices, invalid decisions, and non-System Diagram figures.

items.title: Render
items.text: The renderer fills the sole report template and embeds shared CSS, navigation, decision runtime, DocumentSpec, and template digest.

items.title: Review
items.text: The human reads self-contained HTML and exports review decisions; an agent reconciles only explicitly accepted truth.

sections.title: The renderer seam sees content, figure provenance, and output together

blocks.question: Where does source-owned document meaning become deterministic self-contained HTML?
blocks.caption: One portable renderer validates domain-owned DocumentSpec and System Diagram source/output before filling the sole report template.
walkthrough: PRD or Design Solution supplies required structured meaning.
The DocumentSpec makes approval, decisions, roles, and IDs machine-checkable.
System Diagram supplies retained system-diagram-v1 JSON and generated SVG.
HTML Report Designer validates both and fills one report template.
Invalid authority or provenance blocks; valid input emits deterministic portable HTML.

sections.title: The architecture has one production path

blocks.question: Which module owns report markup, CSS, runtime, and profile validation?

options.label: PRD/design skills hand-author their own reports

blocks.rationale: The renderer sees all presentation concerns and can stay portable and deterministic without weakening domain ownership.

blocks.question: What is the editable source of a durable report?
blocks.rationale: Structured source makes content profiles, approval, decision lifecycle, deterministic regeneration, and review anchors enforceable.

blocks.question: How are diagrams supplied to the report renderer?

options.label: System Diagram supplies retained system-diagram-v1 JSON and generated infrastructure SVG
System Diagram supplies Excalidraw JSON and exported SVG

blocks.rationale: A dedicated deterministic SVG/CSS renderer keeps evidence, geometry, accessibility, provenance, and visual language consistent without a browser export backend.

sections.title: Strict failure is cheaper than silent drift

items: Cost
A new semantic component requires a shared schema/renderer change and focused tests.
Benefit
All document kinds receive the same fixes, styles, controls, and fallbacks.
Failure posture
Invalid roles, approval, decisions, source paths, or provenance fail before output.
Recovery
Correct structured source or restore the declared companion skill; never patch output.
Proof strategy

Positive/negative profile fixtures, template lock, decision runtime test, copied-skill rendering, deterministic checks, System Diagram freshness, and desktop/mobile/no-JS/reduced-motion/print browser checks.

blocks.title: Legacy artifacts
blocks.text: Existing reports remain readable, but new validation rejects them as canonical generation sources until migrated.

sections.title: The renderer remains intentionally ignorant of domain decisions

items: No automatic product or architecture choice from available components.
No implied approval from completeness, browser persistence, passing tests, or prior implementation.
No alternate report template, CSS family, diagram renderer, or hand-authored SVG path.
No task creation, implementation steps, or execution evidence in PRD/design generation.
No external Pi configuration gate inside this repository's default verification command.

blocks.text: The architecture ADR owns the durable single-renderer rationale; this feature design owns the current paths, profiles, and verification consequences.
